h1
Every day, 61,200 vehicles cross the Charles River Dam road bridge by the Museum of Science in Boston.
h2
Built in 1906 and rebuilt in 2011, its substructure and scour protection are each rated four out of nine. That is Poor.
p1
Massachusetts has 5,252 bridges, and 444 of them are rated Poor today.
p2
Those Poor bridges carry about 10.1 million vehicle crossings every single day.
p3
2,600 bridges cross water. 778 need underwater inspection, done by divers today, and 123 are scour critical.
b1
In one day, a team of three built a system that inspects a bridge above and below the water, in simulation.
d1
The drone is a Holybro X500, flown by real ArduPilot through a 38-item mission in AUTO with QGroundControl.
d2
It carries an Ouster 3D lidar, a gimbal RGB camera, floodlights, and a thermal camera, which is labelled simulated.
d3
Over open water it sees 12 satellites. Under the deck, its GPS drops to 7.
d4
So we cannot trust GPS where the inspection matters most, in the shadow directly beneath the bridge.
r1
Below the surface, the ROV is a BlueROV2 Heavy, flown by real ArduSub, with no GPS at all.
r2
It navigates on a Doppler velocity log fed to the autopilot's filter, like the real BlueOS setup.
r3
Its imaging sonar reaches 12 meters across a 130-degree field, beside a low-light camera built for turbid water.
r4
In our test, measured drift was about 0.4 meters after 60 meters of travel.
t1
The two robots work together. The drone flags defects at the water line as it flies.
t2
The ROV is then tasked automatically to dive and inspect the wall directly below each flag.
t3
In our recorded run the drone flagged 4 defects, and the ROV inspected all 4 of them.
t4
The result is one 3D model: 2.96 million lidar points above the water joined to 1.58 million sonar points below.
a1
An AI triage model, built with Kiro, scores all 5,252 Massachusetts bridges for underwater inspection risk from condition, scour, age, and traffic.
a2
Its number 1 is the North Washington Street bridge over the Charles, scour critical, a mile from our site.
l1
To be honest about limits: this runs in simulation, the thermal is simulated, and the defect flags come from ground truth.
c1
Scour is the river eroding the bed around a bridge's foundations, and it is invisible from above the water.
c2
We built a way to see it, so the next inspection can look below the waterline before sending a diver down.
